page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard2.24 is an enterprise compute instance belonging to the Standard family, driven by the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8167M processor operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. The server provisions 24 physical cores mapped to 48 dedicated virtual CPUs via simultaneous multithreading at two threads per core. System memory is scaled to 320.0 GB, yielding a memory density of 6.67 GB per vCPU.

The hardware configuration provides no integrated local disk storage and zero GPU accelerators. All persistent storage requirements, operating system files, and database write targets must be handled through network-attached block storage volumes. Network configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address for external accessibility.

From an architectural standpoint, the 2.0 GHz clock speed emphasizes parallel throughput across 48 vCPUs rather than single-threaded clock frequency. The generous allocation of 320.0 GB of memory supports moderate to high working sets without requiring specialized memory-heavy infrastructure. The absence of local solid-state disks reduces hardware-bound storage coupling, though it necessitates careful provisioning of remote block volumes for disk I/O.

VM.Standard2.24 is suitable for horizontally scaled enterprise application backends, container orchestration nodes, middle-tier services, relational database management systems backed by remote block volumes, and batch ETL pipelines.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard2.24 is a general-purpose compute instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8167M x86_64 processor operating at 2.0 GHz. The configuration provides 24 physical cores and 48 dedicated vCPUs with two execution threads per core, paired with 320.0 GB of system memory, delivering roughly 6.67 GB of RAM per vCPU. This shape includes no local storage or GPU hardware, requiring external network-attached block volumes for system files and persistent data. Networking provisions include one complimentary public IPv4 address. With a substantial memory allocation relative to its 48 vCPUs, the VM.Standard2.24 offers predictable multi-threaded capacity for resource-dense environments. It is well suited for horizontally scaled enterprise application tiers, relational database engines using remote storage, batch processing pipelines, ETL workloads, and general-purpose microservice clusters.
